title: Two Sizes
statement: Implement `solve(t1, t4)`. `t1` is the time at size n and `t4` is the time at size 4n, both positive integers. Return `linear` when t4 is less than or equal to 6 times t1. Return `super` when it is larger. A rough linear curve grows about 4 times. A quadratic curve grows about 16 times. The threshold 6 separates them.
constraints: 6 is the cutoff, inclusive on the linear side
hints: Do not require an exact 4 times ratio.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Two sizes distinguish a linear scan from a quadratic one without a formal fit.

editorial: Two sizes distinguish a linear scan from a quadratic one without a formal fit. Noise means a linear function may land a bit above 4. A quadratic jump is far past 6. The cutoff is a decision rule for a profile, not a proof, and it is good enough to choose which function to read.
